text: Make sure you go somewhere where you have a good engineering partner. Because if you have great ideas of what to build but you can't get them built, then you go nowhere.
speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
context: Lenny asks Tamar about building stronger cross-functional relationships, especially between product managers and engineers. Tamar explains that having a strong engineering partnership is crucial for product success - great ideas mean nothing if they can't be executed. She emphasizes the importance of alignment between product and engineering leaders, where both parties understand their roles and responsibilities and don't undermine each other by giving conflicting direction to their teams.
text_ko: 꼭 좋은 엔지니어링 파트너(engineering partner)가 있는 곳으로 가세요. 만들 아이디어가 아무리 좋아도 그걸 실제로 구현하지 못하면 아무런 진전이 없어요.
text_zh: 一定要去有靠谱的工程伙伴(engineering partner)的地方。要不然你想法再好，落实不了也走不远。
text_es: Asegúrate de ir a un lugar donde cuentes con un buen socio de ingeniería (partner). Porque si tienes grandes ideas sobre qué construir pero no puedes hacerlas realidad, no llegas a ninguna parte.
key_sentence: if you have great ideas of what to build but you can't get them built, then you go nowhere.
original_text: Make sure you go somewhere where you have a good engineering partner. Because if you have great ideas of what to build but you can't get them built, then you go nowhere. So that has to be part of your evaluation criteria that you meet and value your engineering partner before you join. And then I think what's really important is that you're aligned. You understand your roles and responsibilities and where you're going to divide and conquer and where you're going to be aligned. You don't want any of this ... Like people in the organization, they ask mom, they asked dad and they got different opinions and playing one against the other. That doesn't work.

vocabulary.definition: An organization or individual that collaborates with another entity to provide technical expertise and support in the development of products or services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech environments, an engineering partner is crucial for startups seeking to leverage specialized skills and resources to bring innovative ideas to fruition.
vocabulary.nuance: This term implies a collaborative relationship that goes beyond mere vendor-client dynamics, emphasizing shared goals and mutual investment in success.

vocabulary.definition: Innovative and valuable concepts that have the potential to solve problems or create opportunities.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the context of startups and business development, great ideas are often the foundation for new products or services, driving creativity and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'great ideas' suggests high potential, it is important to recognize that execution and implementation are equally critical for success.

vocabulary.definition: The process of constructing or developing a product, system, or structure from initial concept to final implementation.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, 'built' often refers to the actual creation of software, hardware, or services that are ready for market launch or operational use.
vocabulary.nuance: This term conveys a sense of completion and functionality, implying that the product is not just conceptual but has been realized in a tangible form.

text: One of the things that I think is overlooked is do a really good job at whatever your job is at that point. People have a tendency ...
speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
context: Lenny asks Tamar about the specific skills or habits that contributed most to her successful career. Tamar explains that one of the most overlooked but important factors is excelling at your current role rather than constantly focusing on the next promotion. She argues that ambitious product managers often make the mistake of always looking ahead instead of delivering exceptional results in their present position, which is actually the key to advancement.
text_ko: 제가 생각하기에 간과되는 것 중 하나는 그때 맡은 일을 정말 제대로 잘하는 거예요. 사람들은 ...
text_zh: 我觉得常被忽视的一点是，先把当下的工作做好。人们往往会……
text_es: Una de las cosas que creo que se pasa por alto es hacer muy bien el trabajo que tengas en ese momento. La gente tiende a...
key_sentence: do a really good job at whatever your job is at that point.
original_text: One of the things that I think is overlooked is do a really good job at whatever your job is at that point. People have a tendency ... Especially product managers are very ambitious and they want to get to the next level and they're always eyeing the next job, but you're not going to get the next job unless you do really well at the job that you're in. Knock it out of the park. However simple, however easy it may be to you, do a great job.

vocabulary.definition: To fail to notice or consider something, often leading to missed opportunities or insights.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, overlooked aspects can include market trends, employee contributions, or potential risks that may affect decision-making.
vocabulary.nuance: The term often carries a connotation of negligence or lack of attention, suggesting that the oversight could have significant consequences.

vocabulary.definition: An inclination or predisposition to behave in a certain way or to have a particular characteristic.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding tendencies within consumer behavior or team dynamics can help businesses tailor their strategies and improve performance.
vocabulary.nuance: This word suggests a pattern that may not be absolute but is observable over time, making it useful in predictive analyses.

text: One of the things that I caution product managers about is that you don't want to be too overly reliant on metrics and you want to also have an intuition.
speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
context: Lenny asks for an example of understanding people in product development. Tamar discusses the balance between data-driven decisions and product intuition. She explains that while metrics are important, product managers shouldn't rely on them exclusively - they need to develop intuitive understanding of their customers and products. This intuition, when properly developed through deep product knowledge, can guide correct decisions even when data might not provide clear direction.
text_ko: 제가 프로덕트 매니저(product managers)들에게 자주 당부하는 것 중 하나는 지표(metrics)에만 너무 의존하지 말고 직감도 중요하게 여겨야 한다는 거예요.
text_zh: 我常提醒产品经理(product managers)：别过度依赖指标(metrics)，也要保留自己的直觉判断。
text_es: Una de las cosas que les advierto a los responsables de producto (product managers) es que no conviene fiarse únicamente de las métricas; también hace falta tener intuición.
key_sentence: Don't be overly reliant on metrics; trust your intuition.
original_text: One of the things that I caution product managers about is that you don't want to be too overly reliant on metrics and you want to also have an intuition. You want product managers who understand intuitively their customers and their product and sometimes you'll make decisions because you just know it's the right thing to do because it feels right and it usually is right if you understand your product well enough.

vocabulary.definition: Dependent on someone or something for support or assistance.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, being reliant often refers to a company's dependence on specific metrics, technologies, or personnel to make decisions or drive performance.
vocabulary.nuance: While reliance can indicate trust in a system or process, being overly reliant may suggest a lack of critical thinking or adaptability.

vocabulary.definition: Quantitative measures used to assess performance, progress, or quality in various contexts.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business and tech sectors, metrics are crucial for evaluating success, guiding strategy, and making informed decisions based on data analysis.
vocabulary.nuance: While metrics provide valuable insights, an overemphasis on them can lead to a narrow focus that overlooks qualitative factors.

vocabulary.definition: The ability to understand something instinctively, without the need for conscious reasoning.
vocabulary.businessContext: In product management and decision-making, intuition plays a key role in complementing data analysis, allowing leaders to make quick judgments based on experience and gut feelings.
vocabulary.nuance: Intuition can be powerful, but it may also be subjective and less reliable than data-driven approaches, warranting a balanced use of both.

text: I love working at well-run companies. It's more fun, your people are happier. I like running a well-run team, so I aspire to have a very well run team and to work at a well run company.
speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
context: Lenny asks about Tamar's insight that companies don't need to be well-run to win. Tamar explains this seemingly contrarian view by distinguishing between what makes companies pleasant to work at versus what makes them successful. She acknowledges preferring well-run organizations for personal satisfaction, but observes that operational dysfunction - like broken IT systems, poor marketing, inadequate HR, and high turnover - doesn't necessarily prevent business success, while she's also seen well-run companies that fail to grow.
text_ko: 저는 운영이 잘되는 회사에서 일하는 걸 좋아해요. 훨씬 더 재미있고 구성원들도 더 행복해요. 저는 팀을 잘 운영하는 걸 좋아해서 아주 잘 운영되는 팀을 만들고 그런 회사에서 일하고 싶어요.
text_zh: 我喜欢在管理得好的公司工作，工作氛围更轻松、大家也更开心。我也喜欢把团队带得井井有条，所以我希望能打造一个高效运作的团队，也希望能在这样管理到位的公司里工作。
text_es: Me encanta trabajar en empresas bien gestionadas. Se trabaja mejor: es más divertido y la gente está más contenta. Me gusta dirigir un equipo que funcione bien, así que aspiro a tener un equipo muy bien gestionado y a trabajar en una empresa así.
key_sentence: I love working at well-run companies.
original_text: I love working at well-run companies. It's more fun, your people are happier. I like running a well-run team, so I aspire to have a very well run team and to work at a well run company. But what I've seen is when a company isn't well run like IT isn't working, marketing is broken, there are not enough people in HR, there's a lot of turnover. All of these things I've seen that they're not correlated to the company being successful.

vocabulary.definition: Effectively managed or organized, resulting in efficient operations and positive outcomes.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, a well-run company is often characterized by strong leadership, clear processes, and high employee morale, which can lead to increased productivity and profitability.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'well-run' conveys a sense of efficiency and success, it may imply a lack of flexibility or innovation if overemphasized.

vocabulary.definition: To have a strong desire or ambition to achieve something, typically requiring effort and determination.
vocabulary.businessContext: In a corporate setting, individuals may aspire to leadership positions, innovative projects, or company-wide goals that align with their career ambitions.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'aspire' often carries a positive connotation of hope and ambition, but it can also imply a gap between current status and future goals.

text: Really recently I was talking to somebody in their twenties who was asking me for career advice. Should I be a product manager, et cetera.
speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
context: Lenny asks about Tamar's belief that you don't need to plan your career. Tamar shares a recent conversation with someone in their twenties seeking career advice about becoming a product manager and creating a five-year plan. She reveals that she has never had a five-year career plan throughout her successful career, which immediately relieved the anxiety of the person she was advising. This challenges the conventional wisdom that successful careers require detailed long-term planning.
text_ko: 정말 최근에 20대인 분이랑 얘기했는데 커리어 조언을 물어보시더라고요. '프로덕트 매니저(product manager)가 돼야 할까요?' 이런 식의 질문이었어요.
text_zh: 就在最近，我跟一个二十多岁的年轻人聊，他在向我请教职业建议，比如要不要做产品经理（product manager）之类的。
text_es: Hace muy poco hablé con alguien de veintitantos que me pidió consejo sobre su carrera: "¿Debería ser responsable de producto (product manager) o algo así?"
key_sentence: Should I be a product manager, et cetera.
original_text: Really recently I was talking to somebody in their twenties who was asking me for career advice. Should I be a product manager, et cetera. And I'm trying to put together my five-year plan and I said, 'I never had a five-year plan.' So to be clear, some people need that. That's the kind of people they are. They want the planning. I said, 'It's great if you want that, but I never had it.' And the person I was talking to just relaxed and they're like, 'Oh my God, that's so great to hear because I have no idea what I want to do in five years.' I'm like, 'I still have no idea what I want to do in five years. I've never had an idea what I want to do in five years.'

vocabulary.definition: Guidance provided to individuals regarding their professional paths, including choices about education, job opportunities, and career development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, career advice often comes from mentors or HR professionals who help employees navigate their career trajectories and align their skills with organizational needs.
vocabulary.nuance: While career advice is generally constructive, it can sometimes carry an implicit bias based on the advisor's own experiences or industry trends.

vocabulary.definition: A professional responsible for overseeing the development and lifecycle of a product, ensuring it meets market needs and aligns with business goals.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, product managers play a crucial role in coordinating between engineering, marketing, and sales teams to deliver successful products to market.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can imply a blend of technical, business, and interpersonal skills, and is often associated with leadership and strategic thinking.

text: What I believe, and I've always believed is that you follow people. You learn the most from people. I don't look for domains.
speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
context: Continuing the discussion about career planning, Tamar explains her philosophy for career progression without formal plans. Instead of focusing on specific industries or domains, she advocates following exceptional people - those who are genuinely the best at their craft, whether in product thinking, engineering, or sales. She emphasizes that personal likability isn't enough; you need to work with people who excel at their skills so you can learn how to become exceptional yourself.
text_ko: 제가 늘 믿어온 건 사람을 따라가는 거예요. 사람에게서 가장 많이 배워요. 저는 특정 분야(domain)를 찾아다니지는 않아요.
text_zh: 我一直相信，跟对人走最重要。你从人身上学到的最多，我不会去刻意找哪个领域。
text_es: Lo que creo —y siempre he creído— es que hay que seguir a las personas. Se aprende más de la gente. No me fijo en sectores.
key_sentence: You learn the most from people.
original_text: What I believe, and I've always believed is that you follow people. You learn the most from people. I don't look for domains. Some people have a domain, like I'm super interested in climate or whatever and they really want to work in that area and that's fine so maybe within that area. But you follow people who are the best at what they do. So it's not good enough to follow somebody who you like. You want to follow somebody who's either the best product thinker or the best engineer or the best salesperson. And so that you will learn the skill of how to be the best at that.

vocabulary.definition: Specific areas of knowledge, expertise, or activity within a broader field.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startup environments, domains often refer to specialized sectors such as finance, healthcare, or software development, guiding strategic decisions and innovations.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'domains' can imply a level of specialization, suggesting that expertise in one area may not translate to others.

text: I got a piece of advice from a friend that I thought was amazing advice as a leader.
speaker: Tamar Yehoshua
context: Lenny discusses the concept of companies having gravitational pull for talent. Tamar shares advice she received from a friend about leadership job selection. When she was considering various leadership roles, including some turnaround situations, her friend suggested she only take positions where hiring people would advance their careers. This advice made her realize she should evaluate opportunities not just for her own benefit, but for whether she could genuinely help the people she'd recruit to learn and grow.
text_ko: 친구가 해준 조언이 하나 있는데, 리더로서 들으니 정말 인상 깊었어요.
text_zh: 有位朋友给了我一句建议，作为领导我觉得特别受用。
text_es: Un amigo me dio un consejo que, como líder, me pareció increíble.
key_sentence: I got a piece of advice from a friend that I thought was amazing advice as a leader.
original_text: I got a piece of advice from a friend that I thought was amazing advice as a leader. She said to me, 'Take a job where if you hire people, it's going to make their careers.' I was like, 'Whoa.' Because I was getting offers for some turnaround jobs. And if you think you can turn around, great. But if you're going to hire the best people, you want to make sure that it's going to be a good place for them and that they're going to learn and they're going to grow.

vocabulary.definition: Guidance or recommendations offered with regard to prudent future action, often based on experience or expertise.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the business world, advice can come from mentors, consultants, or peers and is vital for decision-making and strategic planning.
vocabulary.nuance: Advice can carry varying degrees of weight depending on the source's credibility and the context in which it is given; it is often seen as subjective.
